6.overview:
Unix permission bits are grouped in three triplets (owner, group, others): r=4, w=2, x=1 summed per triplet. Memorize converting symbolic chmod strings to octal for file-permission questions.

✅ Answer: D — 755

options.A: Option A (INCORRECT): "744". 744 mismatches execute bit for group.
options.B: Option B (INCORRECT): "700". 700 would deny group/other all access beyond owner.
options.C: Option C (CORRECT): "755". 755 = rwxr-xr-- is standard mapping—exam answer.
options.D: Option D (INCORRECT): "766". 766 would require group/other write bits not present.

6.studyTip: Octal: r=4,w=2,x=1 per triplet; add for owner/group/other.

11.overview:

options.A: Option A (INCORRECT): "Broadcast receiver". BroadcastReceiver delivers system-wide or app-wide events asynchronously (e.g., battery low). It is not the idiomatic way to start another Activity with user-specific fields like a username.

options.C: Option C (CORRECT): "Intent". Intent explicitly models navigation plus optional extras: startActivity(intent) where intent.putExtra("key", value). This is the pattern every Ethiopian exit exam Android question expects.
options.D: Option D (INCORRECT): "Content provider". ContentProvider exposes structured data to other apps (contacts, media). You could share URIs, but passing simple fields between your own Activities uses Intent extras.
